symptom: scripts/verify_mutation.sh printed `mutation: PASS` and the Fault injection job went green in 2m0s instead of the usual ~10 min. Buried in the log, a note read `node_modules not found -- the vitest faults will be skipped`; they were not skipped. All three vitest faults reported vitest=CAUGHT, and M15 -- a fault whose whole purpose is to document an undetectable gap -- reported `M15 is now caught -- a gap was closed; change its expectation to 'caught'`. Taking that advice would have deleted a real documented blind spot on the strength of a measurement that never happened.
rootcause: gate() decides detection purely by exit status: any non-zero exit from the gate command counts as the fault being caught. That is sound only while the gate can actually run. .github/workflows/mutation.yml had no Setup Node and no npm ci -- it never needed them until M13-M15 added a vitest gate -- so node_modules was absent, `npx vitest run` exited 1 because vitest was not installed, and every vitest fault was scored CAUGHT without a single test executing. The script's own guard was a warning printed to stderr rather than a hard failure, and its wording was wrong: nothing was skipped, everything was mis-measured. The failure is self-concealing, because the broken direction is the one that looks like success.
fix: Three layers. (1) mutation.yml now runs Setup Node and npm ci, so the gate can execute. (2) verify_mutation.sh exits 1 when node_modules is absent instead of warning and continuing. (3) The general fix: the script now preflights every gate against the unmutated worktree and refuses to run if any is already red, on the principle that a gate failing before a fault is injected cannot distinguish anything. That last check is what catches this class rather than this instance -- a missing interpreter, an uninstalled tool or a bad path in any future gate now stops the suite instead of turning it green.
notes: Found by CI on the very first execution of mutation.yml, which had existed for weeks without ever running because scheduled workflows fire only from the default branch. Same shape as dead-posttooluse-hook: a check whose failure mode is indistinguishable from success. The difference is that this one was worse than silence -- it actively recommended closing a blind spot it had not tested. A local run could not have caught it, because a developer's tree always has node_modules.
